lead.title: Satelia opens its heart failure remote monitoring to digitally excluded patients with a Withings blood pressure monitor that sends readings on its own
lead.deck: Announced on November 25, the first deployments of the Withings BPM Connect Pro within the Satelia Cardio offering automatically send blood pressure and heart rate over the mobile network, with no Wi-Fi or smartphone needed, straight into the follow-up questionnaire reviewed by the cardiologist; the 3G monitor is optional and offered by care teams to patients with poor eyesight or little comfort with digital tools. The stakes are high: 1.4 million adults live with heart failure in France and more than 180,000 are hospitalised each year; the TELESAT PRIOR-HF analysis associates Satelia monitoring with 46% lower mortality and 15% fewer readmissions after a hospital stay, with no significant extra cost to the national health insurer at 6, 12 and 24 months. Removing the usability barrier is the precondition for scaling under standard reimbursement.

milestone.title: The West Midlands Secure Data Environment will lead SENTINEL-AI, national monitoring of the performance of AI deployed across the NHS, on Newton's Tree's platform
milestone.summary: Announced on November 25 with support from the Health Data Research Service, the project brings together University Hospitals Birmingham, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde, Cambridge University Hospitals and CERSI-AI, with Newton's Tree providing the technical platform. It aims to let organisations generate and compare evidence on the safety and effectiveness of AI tools in use without transferring patient-level data; it starts with chest X-ray reading and is set to extend to ambient voice technology, retinal imaging and pathology, with findings due in 2027.
milestone.why: Clinical AI is bought on performance measured before market entry and rarely checked afterwards at health-system scale. A national, federated framework for real-world monitoring creates a new infrastructure layer, and a market for deployment platforms such as Newton's Tree.

deal.thesis: Irish investor Melior Equity Partners is backing ADHD Now and AutismCare, two Cork-based providers that combine online appointments with physical clinics (Cork, Dublin, Limerick, Kilkenny, Donegal) for ADHD and autism assessment and follow-up care: more than 15,000 people treated since 2023, around 100 clinicians, and contracts with the HSE and insurers; co-founders Danny Buckley and Jack Starling remain majority owners. The thesis: with public waiting lists growing, hybrid mental health models that bill the public payer, insurers and private patients are becoming private equity targets, with the money going into clinicians, assessment capacity and technology.

brefsEurope.title: Warburg Pincus-backed Health Partners Group acquires ICE Creates, a specialist in behaviour change programmes and health coaching
brefsEurope.summary: The occupational health provider, which supports more than 6 million client employees in the UK and Ireland, is buying a company founded more than 25 years ago whose health coaching, digital support and population health programmes are commissioned by local authorities and healthcare organisations; terms were not disclosed. The group is moving beyond the workplace into prevention and early intervention.

brefsEurope.title: medishift launches Kira, an AI that builds medical practice rosters on its own and organises cover when staff call in sick
brefsEurope.summary: Built into Lindotech's scheduling software, Kira applies practice rules written in plain language, plans a full week in one pass and asks suitable colleagues to cover via the app; by default every change is approved by the team, with models hosted in the EU and data in Frankfurt. More than 900 practices have signed up since launch in August 2025.

brefsEurope.title: France's health ministry sets up an AI in healthcare advisory board of hospital federations, community care and patients, with no industry members
brefsEurope.summary: Meeting for the first time on November 18 under the 2025-2028 "AI and health data" strategy, it includes the FHF, FHP, FEHAP, Unicancer, France Assos Santé and 100000médecins.org, and will map uses, rank use cases and organise post-deployment "algorithmovigilance" of AI tools. Context: 91% of surveyed health professionals use AI, but only 24% through a secure tool provided by their organisation.

brefsEurope.company: Department of Health and Social Care
brefsEurope.title: The UK's DHSC and Department for Education publish guidance on using AI in children's and adult social care
brefsEurope.summary: Four principles: AI-generated content is a first draft to be reviewed, AI does not make decisions that directly affect people, it must support better outcomes, and no personal information goes into public tools; agentic AI must work within defined boundaries under human oversight. The guidance cites Kingston Council, where social workers save 50% to 60% of the time spent transcribing and drafting.

brefsEurope.title: Chronic wound telemedicine: Domoplaies is still waiting for nationwide rollout, while the ministry says its funding is maintained
brefsEurope.summary: Launched in 2011 and trialled under France's Article 51 scheme, the tele-expertise service for community teams, care homes and hospitals received a favourable opinion for nationwide rollout after a positive clinical and economic evaluation in early 2025; but the transition period was due to end on August 1 and founder Dr Luc Téot says he has heard nothing since and is advancing the costs. A textbook case of how hard it is to move from experiment to standard reimbursement.

brefsEurope.title: DiGA: BfArM president Karl Broich backs fully digital prescription and activation, as activation codes take up to three weeks to reach patients
brefsEurope.summary: At the Bitkom Health conference, DiGA are still prescribed on paper (Muster 16) pending the GeDIG law; Anna Haas (Oviva, deputy chair of SVDGV) argued for real-world data to set reimbursement, against the PNOG plan to cut prices according to early drop-out rates. Broich also said the BfArM has built an internal database to make its advice and decisions more consistent.

brefsEurope.title: At Barts Health, Copilot lifts the patient complaint response rate from 60% to 92% and halves drafting time
brefsEurope.summary: The patient experience team uses it to analyse complaint narratives, draft investigation documents and prepare responses, with every output reviewed and approved by a human; reopened complaints have fallen to "almost zero". Separately, more than 2,000 clinicians have access to Oracle's Clinical AI Agent, already used by 1,350 of them.

brefsEurope.title: Cegedim opens EB6, an HDS V2-certified, SecNumCloud-eligible data centre designed for AI and high-density workloads
brefsEurope.summary: The group's fifth data centre in France, operational since September on a 2.2-hectare site, relies on direct liquid cooling and targets dual Tier IV certification to host the group's healthcare clients in a sovereign cloud. A market signal: AI compute is becoming a selling point for health data hosting in France.

brefsIntl.title: WebMD Ignite launches a ChatGPT advertising offering for US health systems with OpenAI
brefsIntl.summary: The Internet Brands unit runs campaigns end to end, while OpenAI keeps the final say on eligibility, creative approval and delivery; ads are labelled, separated from answers, barred from sensitive health conversations and have no access to chats. A first cardiology campaign is live for an academic medical centre: the chatbot becomes a patient acquisition channel.

brefsIntl.title: Waystar plugs its revenue cycle analytics and eligibility checks into Google Cloud's Gemini for healthcare via an MCP connector
brefsIntl.summary: Built on the Model Context Protocol, the connector lets users query claims and payer payment data in natural language and run real-time eligibility checks from the Gemini workspace; early adopters report up to 75% less time spent on analysis. General-purpose AI agents are opening up to the transactional layers of the revenue cycle.

word.definition: A platform where approved researchers come to analyse health data without ever being able to download it: researchers go to the data, rather than the data going to researchers.

parts.label: Linked, pseudonymised data
parts.role: the foundation: hospital, GP and other care records, non-identifiable by default

parts.label: Controlled analysis space
parts.role: the lab: tools and code used inside the environment

parts.label: Output checking
parts.role: the airlock: only aggregated, checked results leave the environment

how.t: The project and the researcher are approved under the Five Safes framework (safe people, projects, settings, data and outputs), with an ethics opinion and, in England, advice from the Confidentiality Advisory Group.
The researcher works inside the NHS-controlled environment and cannot download or remove patient-level data.
Everything that leaves, whether data, code or results, is checked: only approved outputs, such as aggregates, leave the environment.

word.why: England has made SDEs the default route to NHS data for research and analysis, and the regional network is now complete. The same principle, never moving the data, is now being used to monitor AI in service, as in the SENTINEL-AI project led by the West Midlands SDE, and paves the way for the secondary data use planned under the EHDS. For VCs, value is shifting to the building blocks that make these environments usable: trusted research environments, federated analytics and output-checking tools.

startups.name: Lifebit
startups.use: Federated trusted research environment; selected again by Genomics England in 2026 to build its next research environment, due to open to researchers in 2027

startups.name: Aridhia
startups.use: Digital Research Environment on Azure with inbound and outbound airlocks; powers Great Ormond Street's DRIVE, offered to other organisations since 2025

startups.name: Bitfount
startups.use: Federated analytics and AI that send algorithms to where the data lives, for TREs and SDEs; raised $8M in 2025
